item.title: Influencers Have a Lot to Say About Politics. Many Are Quietly Paid for It.
item.author: Ken Bensinger and Stuart A. Thompson
item.content:encoded: Their videos have proliferated on social media, but the payments are frequently hidden from viewers.

item.title: Bloomberg This Weekend 8/29/2026
item.content:encoded: The news doesn’t stop when markets close. Hosts David Gura, Christina Ruffini and Lisa Mateo bring clarity, context and a bit of humor to the weekend’s biggest headlines, LIVE from New York. Joined by Schwab Head of Macro Research and Strategy Kevin Gordon, Allspring Global Investments Head of Equity Investments Ann Miletti, Child Online Safety Activist Beeban Kidron and Content Creator Macy Gilliam. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Meta Child Safety Deal Puts Rivals on Notice
item.content:encoded: Meta’s child safety settlement includes new protections for young users and is increasing pressure on other social media platforms to adopt similar safeguards. UK House of Lords National Security Strategy Committee member and Online Safety Activist Baroness Beeban Kidron is on Bloomberg This Weekend and says the bigger impact may come from forcing technology companies to take greater responsibility for product design and age verification, rather than relying on children and parents to protect themselves. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: How Meta’s $17.1 Billion Social Media Settlement Came Together
item.author: Cecilia Kang and Eli Tan
item.content:encoded: State attorneys general spent months in negotiations. Then, as its legal losses mounted, the social media giant’s new top lawyer brought a huge settlement to the table.

item.title: Inside the Dangote Family Vision and the Next Era of African Industry
item.content:encoded: What does the future hold for one of Africa's most powerful industrial empires? In this exclusive conversation on Bloomberg Next Africa, Halima, Mariya, and Fatima Dangote sit down to discuss the next generation of leadership at the Dangote Group — from expanding cement production and investing in refining, fertilizer and power to building a family office focused on preserving the family’s legacy for generations. They also discuss creating more value from Africa’s resources at home, the role of partnerships and investment, and plans for a pan-African IPO of the Dangote refinery. Discover how Aliko Dangote’s daughters plan to carry forward their father's legacy through strategic growth, diversification, and long-term wealth preservation. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Chinese Chipmaker CXMT Sues Pentagon to Get Off US Blacklist
item.author: Ville Heiskanen
item.content:encoded: CXMT Corp. filed a lawsuit against the US Department of Defense, seeking removal from a blacklist that identified the Chinese chipmaker as a supporter of the Communist country’s military.

item.title: OpenAI to End Partnership With Cursor After SpaceX Acquisition
item.author: Yi Wei Wong
item.content:encoded: OpenAI said it will end its partnership with Cursor after the AI-coding agent’s acquisition by SpaceX, according to a post on X.

item.title: Affirm CEO: American Consumers Are Healthy
item.content:encoded: Affirm CEO Max Levchin joins Bloomberg Businessweek Daily to discuss the company's recent earnings report, including an upbeat revenue outlook as the short-term loan company sees its most profitable quarter on record. Levchin also discusses recent partnerships, e-commerce growth, and the state of the consumer, saying Affirm customers are "healthy, paying us back on time, and shopping." He speaks with Tim Stenovec and Lisa Mateo. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Prediction Markets Should Be Regulated as Gambling, Appeals Court Says
item.author: Lauren McCarthy
item.content:encoded: The outcome contradicted an earlier appeals court decision. Federal regulators said the split rulings called for resolution by the Supreme Court.

item.title: SentinelOne CEO on Earnings, AI's Cybersecurity Impact
item.content:encoded: SentinelOne co-founder, chairman and CEO Tomer Weingarten discusses earnings and AI Cybersecurity in an interview with Romaine Bostick and Emily Graffeo on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Social Media and the Myth of the Big Tobacco Moment
item.author: David Streitfeld
item.content:encoded: Smoking used to be everywhere, the way Facebook, TikTok, Snap, YouTube and Instagram are now. Society decided to break the habit, but it took a long time.

item.title: What Meta’s $17 Billion Settlement Means
item.author: Cecilia Kang, Nikolay Nikolov, Paul Abowd, Alexandra Ostasiewicz and June Kim
item.content:encoded: Our reporter Cecilia Kang explains Meta’s settlement of a lawsuit claiming that the company’s social media platforms had harmed teenage users.

item.title: Why Countries Are Pushing Social Media Bans Despite Their Flaws
item.author: John Yoon
item.content:encoded: Proposals for curbing social media use among children have wide support, but critics say they are ineffective.

item.title: Meta Shifts the Blame + Do Data Center Bans Work? + The Final HatGPT
item.author: Kevin Roose, Casey Newton, Rachel Cohn, Whitney Jones, Vjeran Pavic, Alyssa Moxley, Dan Powell, Elisheba Ittoop, Marion Lozano and Rowan Niemisto
item.content:encoded: Meta negotiated an unusual provision in their landmark settlement: If TikTok and YouTube also agree to penalties and changes to their products, Meta will pay more.

item.title: Trump Administration’s Blacklisting of Anthropic Was Illegal, Judge Rules
item.author: Sheera Frenkel
item.content:encoded: The government retaliated against the A.I. start-up “for constitutionally protected expressive activities,” a federal judge in California wrote.

item.author: David Yaffe-Bellany and Sharon LaFraniere
item.content:encoded: A legal dispute over the future of Kalshi, Polymarket and others has drawn in the Trump administration, the president’s son and nearly every state attorney general.

item.title: Mark Zuckerberg Wants to Make Sure YouTube and TikTok Share His Pain
item.author: Mike Isaac
item.content:encoded: Meta, the social media giant, agreed to change the way children interact with its apps. That could be trouble if its competitors don’t abide by the same rules.

item.title: OpenAI and 100 Others Warn That Window to Defend Against A.I. Attacks Is Narrowing
item.author: Kate Conger
item.content:encoded: In an open letter, OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and others said that a wave of A.I.-enabled cyberattacks was coming and that organizations and governments needed to prepare themselves.

item.title: What Does $17.1 Billion Mean for Meta?
item.author: Emmy Martin
item.content:encoded: The Silicon Valley company agreed to pay up to $17.1 billion in penalties as part of a landmark settlement with states over social media addiction claims.

item.title: Some Scientists Have ‘Magic Hands’ in the Lab. This A.I. Is Learning Why.
item.author: Carl Zimmer
item.content:encoded: Even the most adept researchers may not know exactly what they do to get successful results. An A.I. model is trying to figure it out by watching every move.

item.title: “Anxious Generation” Author Jonathan Haidt on the Meta Settlement
item.author: Emma Goldberg
item.content:encoded: In “The Anxious Generation,” he laid out the evils of social media for kids. The landmark Meta settlement seems to agree.

item.title: California Lawmakers Pass Plug-In Solar Bill
item.author: Ivan Penn
item.content:encoded: Legislatures in nearly a dozen states have voted to legalize use of the technology, which can help homeowners reduce their rising electricity costs.

item.title: Meta Projected It Could Spend $10 Billion on Anthropic’s A.I.
item.author: Eli Tan and Kalley Huang
item.content:encoded: The social networking giant projected it could spend $10 billion annually on Anthropic’s tools, illustrating the friend-foe relationships underlying the A.I. race.

item.title: US Says China-Linked Hackers Targeted NASA and Fed
item.author: Bloomberg News
item.content:encoded: The US Justice Department said authorities disrupted online infrastructure allegedly used by Chinese state-sponsored hackers to target American government agencies and critical infrastructure.

item.title: Nvidia’s Profit Doubles to $59.69 Billion Thanks to A.I. Spending
item.author: Kalley Huang
item.content:encoded: Quarterly revenue also more than doubled, to $96.22 billion, the company said, topping expectations on Wall Street.

item.title: Bill Gates Is Warning That A.I. Is More Dangerous Than Big Tech Will Admit
item.author: Karen Weise
item.content:encoded: In an hourlong interview, he said his industry was downplaying the risks, which he believes include mass unemployment and bioterrorism.

item.title: Meta to Pay Up to $17.1 Billion in Landmark Settlement Over Social Media Addiction Claims
item.author: Cecilia Kang and Eli Tan
item.content:encoded: The social media giant settled with 47 states, the District of Columbia and U.S. territories, and agreed to make major changes to its products over claims its platforms endangered children.

item.title: What’s Changing For Teens on Instagram and Facebook After Meta Settlement
item.author: Eli Tan
item.content:encoded: Meta agreed to set more time limits and enhance protections in its platforms for young users, but was short on some specifics.

item.title: Gold, Flights, Cryptocurrency: U.S. Vows to Go After More Than Iran’s Oil
item.author: Zane Irwin
item.content:encoded: The United States threatened sanctions for any country or entity that engages with Iran’s gold, digital assets, aviation, shipping and tech industries. Here’s why that matters.

item.title: Instagram Chief Says ‘No Silver Bullets’ for Teen Safety in Bellwether Trial
item.author: Emmy Martin and Cecilia Kang
item.content:encoded: Adam Mosseri testified in a case brought by states that claim the Meta-owned app created addictive features to hook young users.

item.author: Sheera Frenkel
item.content:encoded: Irregular, an Israeli start-up, worked with OpenAI, Anthropic and Meta to assess the security of their A.I. models. It made a mistake. Then the tests went off the rails.

item.title: SpaceX to Spend $100 Billion on Spaceport in Louisiana
item.author: Ryan Mac
item.content:encoded: It would be the rocket company’s second private launch site after Starbase, its headquarters in South Texas.

item.title: E.P.A. Moves to Curb Public Input on Air Pollution Permits for Data Centers
item.author: Maxine Joselow
item.content:encoded: Under the proposal, states would no longer need to provide public notice or solicit comments on air pollution permits for data centers and other projects.

item.title: Laptop Fire on American Airlines Flight Injures at Least One Passenger
item.author: Christine Chung

item.title: How Big Tech Captured American Schools

item.title: Four Years Ago, a Crypto Boss Went Missing. Now His Successor Has.
